claim: After acknowledging varied readings of other nominalizations, CGEL argues that an event noun determines its genitive’s role as firmly as the corresponding verb determines its subject’s, especially where a further complement is overt.
evidence_summary: The mayors’ release dates a signing with today’s, identifies the legislation in an of-phrase and its signer in a by-phrase. Its next sentence explicitly credits Trump with signing. Compare “The president signed the legislation today”. The time is an adjunct in the clause.
finding: Event meaning and an overt theme do not force the external genitive to supply a participant. A distinct position for temporal genitives could explain the example if there is independent evidence for it. Subjecthood for personal genitives remains open.
proposed_wording: An event noun with an overt theme readily permits a participant interpretation for a personal genitive. An external genitive can also locate the event in time, including when both agent and theme are independently expressed.
inference: Does an overt theme force the initial genitive of an event nominal to express a participant?

evidence.source: U.S. Conference of Mayors (29 January 2020). Statement by U.S. Conference of Mayors President on Signing of USMCA Legislation.
evidence.passage: §16.5.2, p. 475, paragraph after [55ib], Ed’s destruction of the file. CGEL calls a different role “hardly possible”, especially with a further complement, and concludes that noun and verb determine the role “to the same extent”. Compare p. 474 [54xvii].
evidence.example: The release says “today's signing of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) implementation legislation by President Trump”. The next sentence names Trump as the person who signed it.
evidence.establishes: The genitive dates the event while both participants are overt. A temporal adjunct expresses its contribution in the corresponding clause. The token leaves the syntax of personal genitives open.
evidence.locator: Washington dateline, opening sentence and first quoted sentence.
